# Marginalia

The first correction appeared in October, in a copy of *The Sea Around Us* that had been on the shelf since before Doreen started at the library. A pencil note in the margin of page 47: *Tides in the Bay of Fundy — check current figures, this edition is outdated.*

Doreen almost missed it. She was shelving returns, half-listening to the radiator clank, when the slant of the handwriting caught her eye. She flipped through the rest of the book. Three more notes, all in the same careful hand. One simply said *lovely sentence* beside a passage about lantern fish.

She should have been annoyed. Writing in library books was vandalism, technically, even in pencil. But the notes were gentle, almost apologetic, and she found herself erasing nothing.

The second book turned up two weeks later: a novel, this time, with a small correction to a date in the author's biography. Then a cookbook with a note about oven temperatures. Then a history of the town itself, *Harborlight: A Century of Salt and Work*, with a pencilled addition on page 112: *The cannery fire was 1963, not 1961
